rv.q: Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content. Although it won’t necessarily please purist fans of the Bard or the band this mashup of Shakespeare’s tragedy and Radiohead’s 2003 album is a short, sharp jolt of adrenaline that may introduce both to a new audience.
But it's been cut in the interests of an imperfect but enthralling new vision.
Whatever it is, though, it's neat to look at and listen to but far too rushed to triumph.
Honestly, I appreciated the new approach (having already seen so many productions) but found myself slightly ambivalent about the production's merits and shortcomings.
One of the most gripping, frenetic and visceral productions this reviewer has ever seen.
Hamlet Hail to the Thief barely lets you catch your breath, whilst looking and sounding incredible.

Radiohead are a useful sauce to disguise something “good for the child,” the adaptation a decent gateway into Shakespeare, but no more than a chaotic experiment for those familiar with the Bard, alas.
"Hamlet Hail to the Thief" is a feral beast. Packed with more innovation than many an interpretation twice its length.
However, while there were very many elements of this work we enjoyed, we didn't feel it came together as a particular coherent whole.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this Radiohead-Shakespeare mashup, with some praising its bold energy and thematic connections, while others find the collision between the Bard and the band's 2003 album uneven, despite powerful live music.
